why: Studio, not park: Coverr only had flat daylight outdoor yoga (parks, seaside), so I took Mixkit's studio series (887 man in a lunge, 890 dancer pose) and chose 890. A woman in a dark top holds Natarajasana against a warm plaster wall cut by diagonal hard-sun light bands. The figure reads as a near-silhouette against the lit wall, low-key and warm, which is the same family as the backlit boxer on the sport poster, and it sits well under the #7E2600 soft-light grade and the #070301 scrim. Calm, no face to camera, no logos, text or watermarks. Loop: a ping-pong of source frames 229-337 (9.55-14.06 s), 216 frames, 9.01 s. She settles deeper into the pose and then eases back, like a slow breath. Both turnarounds sit at local motion minima. Seam step 1.05 vs a median of 0.49, max 1.03, so no crossfade ghosting from the slow camera drift. Scaled 1920 to 1280x720. 887 moves more but needs a reversed lunge, and a crossfade there ghosts because the camera pans. focusX 0.47 keeps the head, arms and raised foot in a portrait crop. The poster is output frame 108, the deepest point of the pose
